extracted.intended_audience: potential subscribers, advertisers, and contributors to The Forerunner (readers of Charlotte Perkins Gilman)
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial and advertising guidelines, scope, and stated purpose for The Forerunner magazine (Charlotte Perkins Gilman) — what it will publish, why, and how advertisements will be handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship policy
rubrics_metrics.description: What is The Forerunner?  It is a monthly magazine... It is written entirely by Charlotte Perkins Gilman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit editorial policy: all content in the magazine is authored by C. P. Gilman (implies no outside submissions or pieces by other authors for this publication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose / tone
rubrics_metrics.description: What is it For?  It is to stimulate thought: to arouse hope, courage and impatience; to offer practical suggestions and solutions, to voice the strong assurance of better living, here, now, in our own hands to make.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content should aim to provoke thought, inspire, urge practical change, and present a confident, solutions-oriented tone focused on improving present life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: What is it about?  It is about people, principles, and the questions of every-day life; the personal and public problems of to-day.  It gives a clear, consistent view of human life and how to live it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on everyday human concerns — both private and public problems — and on clear, consistent presentation of principles and practical living guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of sexes and children
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it a Woman's magazine?  It will treat all three phases of our existence--male, female and human.  It will discuss Man, in his true place in life; Woman, the Unknown Power; the Child, the most important citizen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although concerned with women's issues, the magazine's remit explicitly includes men and children — content should consider all three 'phases' and their social roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideological stance / social purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it a Socialist Magazine?  It is a magazine for humanity, and humanity is social.  It holds that Socialism, the economic theory, is part of our gradual Socialization, and that the duty of conscious humanity is to promote Socialization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine affirms a socialistic perspective as part of its mission; contributors and advertisers should expect explicit promotion of socialization/socialist ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising policy — truth and personal endorsement
rubrics_metrics.description: In its advertising department, under the above heading, will be described articles personally known and used.  So far as individual experience and approval carry weight, and clear truthful description command attention, the advertising pages of The Forerunner will be useful to both dealer and buyer.  If advertisers prefer to use their own statements The Forerunner will publish them if it believes them to be true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertising copy should be based on personal knowledge/use where possible; the editor will accept and print advertiser's own statements only when the magazine believes them to be true — emphasis on truthful, experience-based advertising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising value proposition
rubrics_metrics.description: We have long heard that 'A pleased customer is the best advertiser.'  The Forerunner offers to its advertisers and readers the benefit of this authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ads are positioned as practical, trustworthy recommendations aimed to be useful to both seller and buyer; advertising is expected to be candid and service-oriented rather than purely promotional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Problems department scope and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The department of 'Personal Problems' does not discuss etiquette, fashions or the removal of freckles.  Foolish questions will not be answered, unless at peril of the asker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'Personal Problems' column is reserved for substantial personal/public problems — trivial, frivolous, or purely cosmetic questions are excluded and may be rejected or ridiculed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planned contents / form expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The main feature of the first year is a new book on a new subject... 'What Diantha Did.' this is a serial novel... Among the short articles will appear: [list of essays and topics].  There will be short stories and other entertaining matter in each issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reader/subscriber expectations: each year will include a complete novel, a new book, a serial novel, short stories, numerous short articles, poems, short sermons, comment and review, and the 'Personal Problems' department — a diverse, author-driven mix of fiction, essays, verse, and practical pieces (all by C.P. Gilman).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription/value framing
rubrics_metrics.description: AS TO VALUE: If you take this magazine one year you will have: One complete novel... One new book... Twelve short stories... Twelve-and-more short articles... Twelve-and-more new poems... Twelve Short Sermons... Besides 'Comment and Review'... 'Personal Problems'... And many other things... DON'T YOU THINK IT'S WORTH A DOLLAR?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publisher frames value in concrete deliverables (counts of works per year) to justify subscription price; this is a guideline for how the magazine markets its content and what subscribers may expect.
